key_insight: ScreenCalib uses an ordinary programmable display to calibrate LiDAR–camera extrinsics, replacing dedicated targets with displayed AprilTags and the screen’s physical geometry.
engineering_relevance: It simplifies calibration setup with a single static placement or multiple independent placements, without continuous motion or inter-pose trajectory estimation.
method: Use camera-observed AprilTags to guide extraction of the physical display from LiDAR measurements.
Generate and refine geometric hypotheses, using surrounding scene edges to resolve association ambiguities.
Combine multiple poses through consensus and jointly refine shared extrinsics and tag scale.
evidence_signal: Simulation and experiments on three sensor platforms report better translation accuracy than competitive board-based methods, with joint multi-pose refinement reducing mean rotation and translation errors across all three platforms.
watch_item: Reliable calibration still depends on extracting screen geometry and resolving cross-modal ambiguities, which clutter and weak surrounding scene edges may complicate.
paper_title: Can a Display Be Used for Rapid LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration?
